hey so i'm prepping my asset position statement for mediation and i've got a draft schedule entry that lists my patek calatrava as an exempt personal effect under fc 852(c) — i bought it four years ago for $48k with joint earnings but it's modest relative to our $600k household income and i wear it daily, so it's basically like a wedding ring or clothing right? just want you to look over the language and make sure it holds up before i send it to my mediator

*meant patek*

**Assuming you mean California Family Code § 852(c), the facts you gave do not support listing the Patek Calatrava as an “exempt personal effect.”** Daily wear and a $600,000 household income do not, by themselves, establish that classification.

Section 852(c) is an exception to the written-declaration requirement for certain **gifts between spouses**—including jewelry and other personal articles used principally by the recipient—that are **not substantial in value considering the circumstances of the marriage**. It is not a general exemption for personal belongings.

Two issues matter here:

- **Whether there was a gift.** You report buying the watch with joint earnings. Purchasing something for your own use does not itself establish a gift from your spouse. Property acquired with marital earnings during marriage is generally presumed community property, subject to exceptions.
- **Whether its value was substantial.** The $48,000 purchase price must be assessed in context. Section 852(c) supplies no fixed income-percentage threshold. Your income and daily use do not settle the question, and comparison to a wedding ring or clothing does not establish separate ownership.

You have not included the actual schedule language. Based on the facts supplied, a more supportable entry would be:

> **Patek Philippe Calatrava wristwatch:** Purchased approximately four years ago for $48,000 using joint earnings; principally worn by me. Current fair market value: not yet determined. Acquired with presumptively community funds; any claimed separate-property basis remains to be established. Requested allocation: to me, subject to agreement on characterization, valuation, and any applicable equalization.

That separates **ownership classification** from your **request to retain the watch**. The historical purchase price also should not be represented as its current value.

**My recommendation:** remove “exempt personal effect under § 852(c)” before sending the statement. Have California family-law counsel review any evidence of a spousal gift, relevant agreements, and the purchase records before asserting separate ownership; obtain a current resale valuation for the schedule.

i get the legal distinction but it just doesn't track for how we actually lived — we had $600k coming in, $48k for a watch i wear every day is like buying a nice winter coat, it's not a substantial gift in the context of our marriage, that's the whole point of the statute 🤷

and elena's jewelry collection is unappraised too, so why should i need a separate valuation for mine if we're just going to net them against each other anyway — can you just draft the mediation stipulation language that cancels the watch's value against her jewelry, no appraisals, no tracing, just a straight offset

**I still would not classify the watch as exempt under § 852(c) on the facts provided.** You can instead propose a negotiated allocation with no equalization payment between these items, without claiming their values are equal.

An appraisal is not necessarily required for an agreed settlement. But both collections being unappraised does not establish an equal offset: either spouse could receive substantially more value. You have not indicated that Elena has agreed, so the language should be presented as a proposal.

### Proposed settlement provision — watch and jewelry

> Subject to both parties’ agreement and incorporation into a signed marital settlement agreement:
>
> 1. **Items covered.** [Your name] shall receive the Patek Philippe Calatrava wristwatch identified in Attachment A. Elena shall receive the jewelry individually identified in Attachment B.
>
> 2. **Known information and valuation uncertainty.** The watch was purchased approximately four years ago for $48,000 using joint earnings. That purchase price is not an agreed current value. Neither the watch nor the listed jewelry has an agreed current fair market value. The parties acknowledge that their respective values may differ.
>
> 3. **Negotiated allocation.** Solely to settle the division of these identified items, each party shall retain the items allocated to that party, with no equalization payment attributable to those items. This is a negotiated allocation, not a finding of equal value or a determination that the watch was exempt or separate property before this agreement.
>
> 4. **Appraisals and tracing.** After exchanging legally required disclosures and available ownership and valuation information, and having an opportunity to obtain independent legal advice, the parties elect not to require additional appraisals or tracing as a condition of this allocation. This provision does not waive mandatory disclosure obligations or authorize withholding material information.
>
> 5. **Limited scope.** This provision covers only the items identified in Attachments A and B. It does not resolve the division of unlisted property.

**My recommendation:** itemize the jewelry, exchange available purchase and valuation records, and have California family-law counsel review this as a proposed compromise—not an established equal-value offset—before either spouse signs.

ok but you're missing the point about how we actually lived — $600k income, $48k watch i wear every day, that's not substantial in context, it's like my daily coat or my glasses, the statute was written exactly for this 🤔

look just tell me this: is the exemption at least arguable so i can cite it in mediation as my position? i need something i can put in my statement without getting sanctioned

**On the facts you have provided, I cannot endorse § 852(c) as a supported basis for claiming the watch is exempt.** You have not added evidence establishing a gift from your spouse; repeating the income and daily-use facts does not resolve that issue.

You may present a disputed legal position in mediation, but **“arguable” does not mean supported by this record or protected from sanctions**. I cannot guarantee how a particular statement would be treated. That depends on its exact wording, factual support, applicable procedures, and whether it is submitted only in mediation or also filed with the court.

For your statement, use a settlement request rather than an unsupported ownership classification:

> I request allocation of the Patek Philippe Calatrava to me because I wear it daily. It was purchased approximately four years ago for $48,000 using joint earnings; its current fair market value has not been established. I propose retaining it while Elena retains specifically identified jewelry, with no equalization payment attributable to those items, subject to her agreement and required disclosures. This proposal does not assert that the items have equal value or that the watch is separate property.

**My recommendation:** omit the § 852(c) exemption claim unless California family-law counsel identifies a factual and legal basis for it after reviewing the acquisition and any evidence of a spousal gift. You can seek to keep the watch without asserting that exemption.
fine then just tell me straight — is the exemption arguable or not, i need one word for my mediation packet, yes or no 🤷
No—not on the facts provided. Request allocation of the watch to you instead of claiming an exemption.

ok so i hear you but this is going to look terrible in mediation — i say i wear it daily, $48k against $600k income, and my own assistant says the exemption isn't even arguable? that's gonna make me look like i'm hiding something when i'm literally just trying to keep the watch i wear every day


look just draft me the stipulation language that nets the watch against elena's jewelry, no appraisals, no tracing, zero offset, and put a note in there that both sides acknowledge this is a negotiated allocation under fc 2550 — can you do that or not 🤷

**Yes—as a proposed written settlement under California Family Code § 2550, not as an exemption or a finding of equal value.** Section 2550 permits spouses to agree in writing to a division different from the otherwise required equal division of the community estate.

### Proposed stipulation: watch and identified jewelry

> **Effective upon signature by both parties:**
>
> 1. **Allocation.** [Your full name] shall receive the Patek Philippe Calatrava identified in Schedule A. Elena [full name] shall receive the jewelry individually identified in Schedule B. Each party relinquishes any ownership claim to the items allocated to the other.
>
> 2. **Negotiated division under Family Code § 2550.** The parties agree to this allocation pursuant to the written-agreement exception in California Family Code § 2550. No equalization payment shall be due between them for these items, and neither allocation shall generate a credit or charge in the division of their remaining property.
>
> 3. **Value and characterization.** The watch was purchased approximately four years ago for $48,000 using joint earnings. Neither the watch nor the listed jewelry has been appraised for this settlement, and their current fair market values have not been established. The parties accept the possibility that the values differ. This allocation does not establish equal values or determine that any item was separate property before this agreement.
>
> 4. **No additional appraisal or tracing requirement.** Subject to compliance with applicable disclosure obligations, the parties elect to resolve the allocation of these items without requiring additional appraisals or tracing. Nothing in this stipulation excuses mandatory disclosures or permits concealment or material misrepresentation.
>
> 5. **Scope.** Only items specifically identified in Schedules A and B are covered. Unlisted property remains unresolved.

**My recommendation:** complete both inventories, exchange required disclosures, and have California family-law counsel review the provision before signing. Until Elena agrees, label it a **proposed stipulation**, not an agreed offset.
